message.content:
Search this repository (/bench/repo) for anything related to caching, Redis, and cache TTL/expiration, especially for "user" entries.

Specifically investigate:
1. Is there any Redis usage anywhere? Search for "redis", "Redis", "ioredis", "REDIS_URL", etc.
2. Where is the cache layer configured? Search for cache implementations, cache config, LRU caches, in-memory caches, etc.
3. Any TTL / time-to-live / expiration settings, particularly for user entries/user cache.

Report exact file paths and line numbers, and quote the relevant code. If Redis is NOT used, say so explicitly and describe what the actual caching mechanism is instead. Be thorough and cite everything.

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
## Findings

This is the **memos** project (Go backend, React/TS frontend). I searched exhaustively across the whole repo.

### 1. Redis: NOT used anywhere

There is **no Redis** in this repository. Confirmed by:
- `grep -rniE "redis|ioredis|REDIS_URL"` across all source returned **zero hits** (the only matches in my broad grep were unrelated Go protobuf `sizeCache`/`SizeCache` struct fields, which are protoc-generated, not caching).
- No `redis`, `ioredis`, or `memcache` dependency in `/bench/repo/go.mod`, `/bench/repo/go.sum`, or `/bench/repo/web/package.json`.
- No Redis references in the frontend at `/bench/repo/web/src`.

There is no external cache server, no `REDIS_URL`-style env var, and no network cache client of any kind.

### 2. The actual cache layer: a custom in-memory TTL cache

The caching mechanism is a hand-rolled, thread-safe, in-process in-memory cache backed by `sync.Map`.

- **Implementation:** `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go`
  - `Cache` struct (lines 66-73) uses a `sync.Map` (`data`) plus an atomic item counter, with a background cleanup goroutine.
  - `Config` struct (lines 41-54): `DefaultTTL`, `CleanupInterval`, `MaxItems`, `OnEviction`.
  - Each `item` (lines 34-39) stores `value`, `expiration time.Time`, and approximate `size`.
  - `New` (lines 76-85) spawns `go c.cleanupLoop()`.
  - Note: side of `golang-lru/v2` appears in `go.sum` (lines 136-137) as an available module, but it is **not** imported by this cache — this is a bespoke implementation, not an LRU library. (The `cleanupOldest`/eviction here is oldest-expiration based, not true LRU.)

- **Wiring / config:** `/bench/repo/store/store.go`
  - The `Store` holds three caches (lines 26-29): `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache`.
  - `New` (lines 38-61) builds the `cache.Config` and instantiates all three via `cache.New(cacheConfig)`.
  - `Close` (lines 72-79) stops each cache's cleanup goroutine.

### 3. TTL / expiration settings — including the user cache

**The user cache uses the default 10-minute TTL.** There is no user-specific TTL override; all three store caches (including `userCache`) share the same `cacheConfig`.

Two places define identical default config values:

`/bench/repo/store/store.go` lines 40-45 (the config actually used at runtime):
```go
cacheConfig := cache.Config{
    DefaultTTL:      10 * time.Minute,
    CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute,
    MaxItems:        1000,
    OnEviction:      nil,
}
```

`/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go` lines 57-64 (`DefaultConfig()`, same values):
```go
return Config{
    DefaultTTL:      10 * time.Minute,
    CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute,
    MaxItems:        1000,
    OnEviction:      nil,
}
```

How TTL/expiration is applied:
- `Set` (cache.go lines 92-95) delegates to `SetWithTTL` using `DefaultTTL` (10 min). A per-entry `SetWithTTL` (lines 97-120) exists but **no caller in the store passes a custom TTL for users** — every user write uses plain `Set`.
- Expiration stamped at write: `expiration: time.Now().Add(ttl)` (line 112).
- Lazy expiration on read: `Get` (lines 135-144) deletes and misses if `time.Now().After(itm.expiration)`.
- Active expiration: `cleanupLoop` (lines 200-215) ticks every `CleanupInterval` (5 min) and `cleanup` (lines 218-250) removes expired items.
- Capacity eviction: when count exceeds `MaxItems` (1000), `cleanupOldest` (lines 253-313) drops ~20% by oldest expiration.

### User cache usage specifically

`/bench/repo/store/user.go`:
- `userCacheKey(userID int32)` — key is just the stringified user ID (lines 88-90).
- Populated on `CreateUser` (line 98), `CreateUserIfNoUsers` (line 122), `UpdateUser` (line 132), `ListUsers` (line 143), and `GetUser` (line 167).
- Read in `GetUser` — only when looking up by `ID` (lines 150-155).

`/bench/repo/store/user_delete.go` lines 39-47 — `deleteUserCache` invalidates the user entry and its per-key user-setting entries.

Related caches sharing the same config/TTL:
- User settings: `/bench/repo/store/user_setting.go` (Set at lines 59, 78, 106; Get at 86-87; Delete at 122), keyed by `getUserSettingCacheKey(userID, key)` = `"%d-%s"` in `/bench/repo/store/cache.go` lines 7-9.
- Instance settings: `/bench/repo/store/instance_setting.go` (`cacheInstanceSetting` lines 166-170, Get at 146-147).

Tests: `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache_test.go`.

### Summary
Redis is **not** used. Caching is a custom in-process in-memory `sync.Map`-based cache (`store/cache/cache.go`) with TTL, periodic cleanup, and max-item eviction. User entries live in `userCache` with the shared **default TTL of 10 minutes**, a 5-minute cleanup interval, and a 1000-item cap — no user-specific TTL override exists.
